title: Complete straightedge-and-compass programs that generate independently bound diagrams
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED, NOT SELECTED: interpret a complete passage as a finite geometric construction program; its execution predicts every represented primitive and its metric relations. This differs from assigning names to a graph or selecting a similar historical picture. Euclid's Elements provides a real historical text-and-construction tradition, including the digitized D'Orville 301 witness described by the Clay Mathematics Institute (https://www.claymath.org/online-resources/euclids-elements/), but no Euclidean Voynich identification or historical encoding key follows. GDT878, GDT213 and GDT221 leave construction ownership and transfer unresolved. No target image, measurement or fit was performed.

design.mechanism: The fixed typed language has JOIN(point,point), CIRCLE(center,point), INTERSECT(object,object,branch) and STOP. Two independently bound seed points normalize to (0,0) and (1,0); every later point, line and circle is created by a prior instruction and addressed by creation index. A branch bit selects the two intersections by a frozen oriented-coordinate convention. Degenerate or undefined instructions reject the program. One complete written group serializes one opcode and its canonical decimal operand indices with fixed separators. One global injective symbol key encodes this finite alphabet across all passages. There are no free coordinates after the seed frame, arbitrary auxiliary deletions, per-diagram object permutations, learned word meanings or unconsumed text groups. The serializer is an explicit unverified hypothesis.
design.unit: A complete passage and a complete independently bounded construction diagram. The output consists of every created primitive; similarities of the whole seed frame are harmless coordinate changes, while arbitrary per-point displacement is forbidden.
design.contrast: Beyond graph isomorphism or GDT878-style conjunctions of visual features, straightedge-and-compass execution forces algebraic metric equalities, intersection positions and a causal construction order. Two incidence-isomorphic diagrams can disagree with those metric predictions. GDT213's medical-diagram scope and GDT221's local construction assignment do not establish such execution; geometric proximity remains insufficient to bind prose or seed operands.
design.prediction: With one globally fixed decoder and independently identified seed points, decode every group of a separately bounded passage before inspecting its output diagram. The resulting program predicts the whole diagram, including previously unseen point positions and all represented auxiliary primitives. A definite impossible reference, missing required primitive or independently measured metric contradiction refutes that complete construction. Measurement tolerance and whether the historical drawing is intended as metric must be fixed independently; schematic drawing cannot be retrospectively treated as failed exact geometry. A successful fit requires all surviving code keys to agree on the predicted construction.
design.scope: A complete geometric meaning would be an operational reading, not unique prose or a claim of Euclidean origin. No current authorial seed marks, complete primitive census, target ownership or justified metric-error model are established. Without them this remains unselected. Source-only confirmation of a bounded historically real construction syntax, together with independently owned diagram input/output structure, is the decisive selection requirement; another count resemblance is not.
